$comment: The two commands this app writes into a .mcfunction, and the limits that decide how.
Generated and maintained by the `mc-commands` skill (.claude/skills/mc-commands).
`node scripts/gen-command-syntax.mjs` turns this into the tables in
src/shared/command_syntax.ts; editing those by hand is fine right up until someone
Two kinds of fact live here and they are not held to the same standard.
The **syntax** is mechanically detectable: the writer emits it, the reader parses it
back, and tests/formats.ts fails if the two disagree. One source is enough, because a
wrong answer cannot survive a round trip.
The **limits** are not. A file that exceeds max_command_sequence_length is truncated by
the game with no error, and one whose fill exceeds max_block_modifications simply does
not place those blocks. Nothing in this repo can see either. So those are corroborated,
and the app writes strictly inside them.
`sinceDataVersion` is what the app actually compares against, because a document carries
a DataVersion rather than a release name. It must agree with resources/mc_versions.json;
the generator refuses if it does not.

forms.note: The mode word is left off on purpose: omitted means `replace`, which is what a schematic wants, and it is the one spelling every release from 1.13 accepts. 1.21.5 added `strict` as a further option without touching this form.
evidence: History: 1.11 (16w32a) added block state support; 1.21.5 (25w02a) added the strict option

forms.note: Same reasoning as setblock. 1.21.5 made `replace` non-terminal and added `strict`; both are relaxations, so the bare form kept working.
evidence: History: 1.11 (16w32a) added block state support; 1.21.5 (25w02a) replace no longer terminal, strict added

forms.note: The namespace may be left off and defaults to `minecraft:`. Flattened ids arrived with 1.13, which is what makes that the floor rather than 1.11, when the bracket syntax itself was added.
evidence: wiki: the block argument format is block_id[block_states]{data_tags}, both optional

limits.name: max_command_sequence_length
limits.note: Commands past it are ignored, with no error. This is why a large build is split across files with a dispatcher rather than written as one.
evidence: wiki-function: the total number of commands run inside a function obeys max_command_sequence_length, 65,536 by default; any beyond it are ignored

limits.name: max_block_modifications
limits.note: A fill past it places nothing and says nothing useful, so no box this app writes may exceed it.
evidence: wiki-gamerule: default 32768, introduced 1.19.4 (23w03a) as commandModificationBlockLimit, renamed max_block_modifications in 25w44a
wiki-fill: the volume limit is controlled by that game rule
